title: U.S. House · Mississippi's 2nd District
area: The Mississippi Delta and parts of Jackson

context.text: Bennie Thompson defeated Evan Turnage and Pertis Williams III in the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary. Ron Eller defeated Kevin Wilson in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Bennie Thompson has represented Mississippi's 2nd Congressional District since a special election in April 1993. A native of Bolton, he was a civil rights movement organizer and a local official in Bolton and Hinds County before entering Congress. He chaired the House Committee on Homeland Security from 2007 to 2011 and from 2019 to 2023, and chaired the House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol.

background.text: Born in 1948 and a native of Bolton, Mississippi.
Earned a B.A. in political science from Tougaloo College and an M.S. in educational administration from Jackson State University.
Before his political career, worked as a school teacher.

According to his official biography, he joined the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee at Tougaloo and served as a field organizer for Fannie Lou Hamer's 1964 congressional campaign, helping lead voter registration drives.
Served as an alderman of Bolton from 1969 to 1972 and as mayor of Bolton from 1973 to 1980, according to his official biography.
Served on the Hinds County Board of Supervisors from 1980 to 1993.
Was elected to the U.S. House in a special election on April 20, 1993, and is serving his 17th term.

Chaired the House Committee on Homeland Security from 2007 to 2011 and from 2019 to 2023, and is now its ranking member; his official biography also lists service on the Agriculture, Budget, and Small Business committees.
In July 2021, Speaker Nancy Pelosi appointed him chairman of the Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol.

His official biography lists the NAACP Chairman's Award (2023) and the Presidential Citizens Medal (2025), and says he authored the 2000 legislation that established the National Center for Minority Health and Health Care Disparities.
According to his official biography, he is married to London Johnson Thompson and is a lifetime member of Asbury United Methodist Church.

priorities.text: Has focused on emergency management, citing his role restructuring FEMA after its handling of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita.
Lists health care as a continuing priority for Mississippi.
Has worked on civil rights issues throughout his tenure.

positions.summary: Opposed repealing the Affordable Care Act and highlights the coverage it extended to uninsured residents of Mississippi's 2nd District.
positions.quote: Congressman Thompson cast a vote against a repeal of the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Supports investing in clean, renewable energy as part of a shift away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: To create the next generation of clean energy jobs, make our nation more secure and reduce the pollution that causes global warming, Congressman Thompson and Congressional Democrats are committed to investing in our nation's clean energy future.

record.text: Chaired the House Committee on Homeland Security during the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
Chaired the House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol.

summary.text: Ron Eller is a retired U.S. Army officer and a cardiothoracic physician assistant and perfusionist who owns a business. He won the March 10, 2026 Republican primary. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes his priorities as free enterprise, limited government, border security, and term limits.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, says he grew up in a working-class, single-parent household in West Virginia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Oklahoma at Oklahoma City (1991) and a master's degree from the University of Nebraska (1998).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1979 to 1999; describes himself as a retired captain who began as an Army combat medic and later served as a squad leader, platoon sergeant, and medical officer.

Works as a cardiothoracic physician assistant and perfusionist with St. Dominic Hospital and is CEO of Buck Warrior Enterprises, LLC; says he helped establish the cardiac surgery program in Vicksburg.
Served as director at large of the Mississippi Academy of Physician Assistants and says he chairs the Mississippi chapter of U.S. Term Limits.
Defeated Kevin Wilson in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary for the 2nd District, 51.1% to 48.9%.

priorities.text: Describes himself as a 'blue collar guy' running against career political elites, saying elected officials often lack real-world experience.
priorities.quote: I am blue collar guy and not part of political elite that wishes to divide us the little people so that they can hold the reins leadership over us.

priorities.text: Lists economic development, border security, education, and limited government/taxation among his policy priorities.
Serves as Mississippi chairman for Term Limits, an organization advocating for congressional term limits.

summary.text: Bennie Foster Jr. is an educator and business owner raised in Jackson, Mississippi, running as an independent. He describes decades of work creating youth programs in violence intervention, music and art, business incubation, and ministry. He says he returned to Jackson about five years ago and is running on a 'People Over Politics' message.

background.text: Says he was raised in Jackson, Mississippi.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Jackson State University and graduated from Strayer University.
Describes spending decades as an educator, creating programs in youth violence intervention, music and art, business incubation, and ministry.
Says he and his wife lived in Florida before he returned to Jackson about five years ago.
Is running for the 2nd District seat as an independent in the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Campaign theme "People Over Politics": says the district is failing because of broken systems and calls for accessibility and accountability from elected leaders.
priorities.quote: People Over Politics. Great success is not a secret, it's a system. Our district is failing because of broken systems.

priorities.text: Campaign theme "Results over Rhetoric": criticizes current leadership for what he calls grandstanding rather than problem-solving.
Says he wants to empower local leaders across the district's 28 counties.
